messages.subject: Identical AIC values for multiple models
parts:
Hi all,
  I have some point count data that I am using to estimate bird densities.  Our initial analysis is set up to explore different detectability models, so I have run a candidate set with half-normal, hazard, and uniform detection functions.  I am getting warning messages (NANs produced) for a few models, but most are running without error.  However, the results don't make sense to me when I run modSel.  To give you an idea, I have reproduced part of the AIC table here:

HN_StateYearLand 7 2212.43 0 0.59
HN_Global 8 2213.14 0.71 0.41
HN_Land 3 2230.29 17.87 0.00
HN_State 5 2242.15 29.73 0.00
HN_Time 3 2263.66 51.24 0.00
HN_Null 2 2265.21 52.78 0.00
HN_Year 3 2266.05 53.63 0.00
U_Null 1 2477.54 265.12 0.00
HZ_Null 3 2479.54 267.12 0.00
U_Year 1 2479.54 267.12 0.00
U_Time 1 2479.54 267.12 0.00
U_Land 1 2479.54 267.12 0.00
HZ_Time 4 2481.54 269.12 0.00
HZ_Land 4 2481.54 269.12 0.00
HZ_Year 4 2481.54 269.12 0.00

Notice that the half-normal models appear to be working fine but the hazard and uniform models produce identical AIC values for models that have the same number of parameters.  This would suggest that the putative detection covariates are meaningless, but that is not the case for the half-normal models and even if it were so, there should be a little bit of noise in the likelihood values.  

Here is a sample of the code I used to specify the models:
HZ_Null<-distsamp(~1 ~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HZ_State<-distsamp(~state~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HZ_Year<-distsamp(~year~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HZ_Time<-distsamp(~min_since_sunrise~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HZ_Land<-distsamp(~land_detect~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
HN_Null<-distsamp(~1 ~1,keyfun="halfnorm", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HN_State<-distsamp(~state~1,keyfun="halfnorm", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HN_Year<-distsamp(~year~1,keyfun="halfnorm", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HN_Time<-distsamp(~min_since_sunrise~1,keyfun="halfnorm", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        HN_Land<-distsamp(~land_detect~1,keyfun="halfnorm", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf) 
 U_Null<-distsamp(~1 ~1,data=umf, keyfun="uniform",output="density",unitsOut="ha")
        U_State<-distsamp(~state~1,data=umf,keyfun="uniform",output="density",unitsOut="ha")
        U_Year<-distsamp(~year~1,keyfun="uniform", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        U_Time<-distsamp(~min_since_sunrise~1,keyfun="uniform", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
        U_Land<-distsamp(~land_detect~1,keyfun="uniform", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf) 

Have I done something wrong?

Thanks,

Andrew Cox
University of Missouri - Columbia

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Identical AIC values for multiple models
parts:
Dear Andrew,

I bet that these models did not converge and that the optimiser got stuck at some local extremum. You could try to go from one model to a "neighbouring" one by using solutions from one as starting values for the next.

Kind regards  --  Marc

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Identical AIC values for multiple models
parts:
Hi Marc,
  That worked perfectly for the hazard function models!  Thanks so much.  I am still unclear on why the models with a uniform detection function do not appear to be working.  It is my understanding that the detection function specifies uniform detectability with respect to distance, but that covariates can still be used to model detectability.  And yet the number of parameters is always listed as 1 even though the AIC scores are adjusted based on the actual number of parameters in the model.  I am not getting any errors or warnings when I run these models.

Andrew

Dear Andrew,

I bet that these models did not converge and that the optimiser got stuck at some local extremum. You could try to go from one model to a "neighbouring" one by using solutions from one as starting values for the next.
